name: Same operation across sets
statement: \text{Find the rule } f \text{ with } f(\text{given}) = \text{result in every complete set; apply } f \text{ to the open set.}
derivation: Start with the complete set that has the smallest numbers.
Try the usual operations in order: sum or difference with a constant, product, product divided by a constant, squares, $\times k\pm c$.
Keep a rule only if it gives the result in every complete set.
For a chain (a - b - c - d) find one operation per step that fits both given chains, then test each option step by step.
shortcut: Compare results with products and sums first: $\frac{ab}{c}$ or $ab - c$ being a small whole number usually shows the rule.
common_traps: Fitting a rule to one set only; it often fails on the second set.
Splitting numbers into digits when the note forbids it.
Accepting an option that fits the first steps but not the last (B: $86+15\neq100$).

verification.code:
from fractions import Fraction as F

# candidate rules for a triad (a, b) -> c
TRIAD_RULES = {}
for k in range(1, 11):
    TRIAD_RULES[f"a*b/{k}"] = lambda a, b, k=k: F(a * b, k)
    TRIAD_RULES[f"(a+b)*{k}"] = lambda a, b, k=k: (a + b) * k
    TRIAD_RULES[f"(a-b)*{k}"] = lambda a, b, k=k: (a - b) * k
for k in range(-20, 21):
    TRIAD_RULES[f"a*b+{k}"] = lambda a, b, k=k: a * b + k
    TRIAD_RULES[f"a+b+{k}"] = lambda a, b, k=k: a + b + k
    TRIAD_RULES[f"a^2+b+{k}"] = lambda a, b, k=k: a * a + b + k

def triad_rules(sets):
    return [n for n, f in TRIAD_RULES.items() if all(f(a, b) == c for a, b, c in sets)]

# candidate single steps for a chain x -> y
STEP_OPS = [("+", k) for k in range(-50, 51)] + [("*", k) for k in range(2, 6)]

def step(op, x):
    return x + op[1] if op[0] == "+" else x * op[1]

def chain_rules(chains):
    """For each step position, the operations that fit every given chain."""
    n = len(chains[0]) - 1
    return [[op for op in STEP_OPS if all(step(op, c[i]) == c[i + 1] for c in chains)] for i in range(n)]

def chain_fits(rule, chain):
    return all(any(step(op, chain[i]) == chain[i + 1] for op in ops) for i, ops in enumerate(rule))

# worked example 2024-09-25_1230_R09: +25, x2, +15
rule = chain_rules([(8, 33, 66, 81), (11, 36, 72, 87)])
assert ("+", 25) in rule[0] and ("*", 2) in rule[1] and ("+", 15) in rule[2]
opts = {"A": (21, 46, 82, 107), "B": (18, 43, 86, 100), "C": (15, 40, 80, 95), "D": (6, 31, 62, 97)}
assert [k for k, c in opts.items() if chain_fits(rule, c)] == ["C"]
# 2024-09-26_0900_R13: +2, -3, +4
rule = chain_rules([(17, 19, 16, 20), (22, 24, 21, 25)])
opts = {"A": (11, 13, 10, 15), "B": (15, 17, 14, 18), "C": (18, 20, 16, 14), "D": (16, 18, 12, 16)}
assert [k for k, c in opts.items() if chain_fits(rule, c)] == ["B"]
# 2024-09-25_0900_R02: (a*b)/3
rules = triad_rules([(24, 15, 120), (21, 19, 133)])
assert rules == ["a*b/3"]
opts = {"A": (31, 9, 96), "B": (18, 16, 99), "C": (27, 12, 108), "D": (33, 10, 170)}
assert [k for k, s in opts.items() if triad_rules([s]) and set(rules) & set(triad_rules([s]))] == ["C"]
